exposure: Mothers' venous blood C-reactive protein (CRP) concentrations
Cervical canal swabs culture for bacteria and fungi
Cervical canal swabs PCR for Ureaplasma urealyticum
Cervical canal swabs PCR for Mycoplasma hominis
Cervical canal swabs PCR for Chlamydia trachomatis
Amniotic fluid culture for aerobic and anaerobic bacteria
Amniotic fluid PCR for atypical pathogens
outcome: Intra-amniotic infection (IAI) confirmed in histopathological examination
cohort: The study included 70 patients who all gave birth by cesarean section, divided into a study group with histologically confirmed IAI (n=34) and a control group without IAI (n=36).
finding: The best predictive values for Intra-amniotic infection (IAI) confirmed in histopathological examination were amniotic fluid glucose and vaginal fluid IL-6 determinations, while mothers' serum CRP and PCT assessments had poor diagnostic value.
